text: When designing REST APIs, it is important to follow some best practices. First, keep your endpoints simple and easy to understand. Use clear names that describe the resource, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients know what happened. For example, use 200 for success and 404 when something is not found. Third, write good documentation so other developers can learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, to keep old clients working when you make changes. These simple rules help you build APIs that are reliable, easy to maintain, and pleasant for others to work with.
